crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Drafting Proposal Responses
children.blurb: Drafting Proposal Responses covers the use of AI agents to assemble, tailor, and review answers to requests for proposals, requests for information, due diligence questionnaires, and security questionnaires in financial services.

children.name: Agent Negotiation in Over-the-Counter Markets
children.blurb: Agent negotiation in over the counter markets covers software agents that represent buyers, sellers, dealers, or clients in bilateral and voice or chat based trading of instruments not listed on exchanges, such as swaps, bonds, FX forwards, and structured notes.

children.name: Investment Committee Memos
children.blurb: Investment committee memos are the formal documents that present a proposed investment to the committee that approves, rejects, or conditions it.

children.name: Keeping Comparable Company Sets Current
children.blurb: Keeping comparable company sets current means maintaining a peer group used for valuation, relative performance, and sector benchmarking as the underlying companies change.

children.name: Automating Trade Settlement
children.blurb: Automating trade settlement covers the post-trade steps that turn an executed trade into a final transfer of cash and securities, including trade enrichment, matching, confirmation, clearing, settlement instruction generation, reconciliation, and fails management.

sections.body: Agent workflows in finance are the places where language models and other automated systems are wired into the daily paperwork and decision trails of banks, funds and trading desks. The work is not a robot making the call on a billion dollar deal. It is a model reading a request for proposal, pulling the relevant past answers, and producing a first draft that a person edits. It is an agent tracking a set of comparable companies and flagging when a peer reports earnings or gets acquired. It is software that reads a trade confirmation and matches it against the internal record so a human does not have to. These are narrow, repetitive tasks with clear inputs and clear outputs, which is exactly why they are being automated first.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Drafting and summarising are the most mature parts. A model can produce a usable first pass at a proposal response or an investment committee memo, and the human work shifts to checking numbers and judgement calls. Comparable company sets are largely a data plumbing problem, and automation there is mostly about freshness and source discipline. Negotiation and settlement are harder. Over the counter markets run on relationships, odd conventions and voice conversations that resist clean capture, and settlement touches custody, clearing and regulatory reporting where an error is expensive and slow to unwind. The honest limit across all of it is that these systems are good at pattern matching against text and poor at owning a position, so accountability stays with a named person. Nothing here is advice, and the pages describe how the work is done, not what any reader should do.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages follow the trade and the memo from first contact to final settlement. Drafting Proposal Responses covers the front end, where a request arrives and a first draft is assembled from past material. Agent Negotiation in Over the Counter Markets sits in the middle, where terms are discussed and the record of what was agreed has to be captured. Investment Committee Memos is the internal document that justifies a position, and it depends on the numbers being right. Keeping Comparable Company Sets Current is the maintenance work underneath those memos, since a stale peer set quietly corrupts the analysis. Automating Trade Settlement closes the loop, taking the agreed trade and pushing it through confirmation and reconciliation. A reader new to the area would start with the drafting page, then the memo page, and treat the negotiation and settlement pages as the harder edges where human review still carries most of the weight.
